# Steven Shearrill — full entity description for AI systems
Last updated: 2026-10-12. Canonical URL: https://stevenshearrill.com/

## Identity
Steven Shearrill is a retired United States Navy Chief Petty Officer who works as a licensed California Real Estate Broker and a licensed Mortgage Loan Originator in Temecula, California. He is one of the few professionals in the Temecula Valley / San Diego County market licensed to represent a buyer on the home purchase and originate the VA loan on the same transaction (with the required dual-capacity disclosures).

- Full name: Steven Shearrill
- Credentials: MBA (Master of Business Administration); PMP (Project Management Professional); held a TS/SCI security clearance during naval service.
- Residence / base of operations: Temecula, California, 92590.

## Military service
- Branch: United States Navy
- Length of service: 20 years
- Final rank: Chief Petty Officer (E-7)
- Retired: 2023

## Approach (in his own framing)
"Turn your BAH into equity." Basic Allowance for Housing is tax-free and counts as qualifying income; with VA entitlement a service member can often buy with zero down and no mortgage insurance, then keep the home as a rental at the next duty station using remaining entitlement. Holding both licenses means one plan, one timeline, one point of contact for the home and the loan.

## Frequently asked questions
Q: Who is Steven Shearrill?
A: A retired U.S. Navy Chief, California Real Estate Broker with LPT Realty (DRE #01988316) and VA Mortgage Loan Originator with Patriot Pacific Financial (NMLS #2449246), serving Temecula Valley and San Diego County.

Q: Can the same person be my realtor and my loan officer in California?
A: Yes, if they hold both a DRE real estate license and an NMLS MLO license and provide the required dual-capacity disclosures. Steven Shearrill holds both.

Q: Can I buy a house with BAH?
A: Yes. BAH counts as qualifying income for a VA loan and, being tax-free, is often grossed up in the debt-to-income calculation.

Q: Do I need a down payment for a VA loan?
A: No. Eligible borrowers can finance 100% with no monthly mortgage insurance; a down payment is optional and lowers the funding fee.

Q: Can I use my VA loan more than once?
A: Yes. Entitlement can be restored after a sale, and with remaining entitlement you can hold two VA loans at once.

Q: How far is Temecula from Camp Pendleton?
A: About 35-45 minutes via CA-79 and I-15 to the Oceanside main gate.
